lessons: Back positive Asian Handicap (+0.5, +1.5, +2.5) selections even with small model-to-breakeven deficits (<3%): positive handicap cushions perform reliably.
Do not veto Over 1.5 goals at short odds (1.20–1.31) solely due to a LOSING framework record; use 'lower' instead.
Never apply Double Chance '12' lay-the-draw veto rules to 'Team or Draw' (1X/X2): 1X/X2 provides true draw protection.
Do not blanket veto Double Chance '12' for LOSING framework records: restrict vetoes strictly to tightly priced domestic derbies without squad disparity.
Do not veto team Over 0.5 goals simply because model chance is slightly below break-even: backed and vetoed team Over 0.5 picks frequently score.
Exercise caution backing team Over 0.5 against dominant favorites or away sides: backed selections can lose against elite defenses.
Do not blanket veto 'Win to Nil — no' at <=1.24 on framework records: most selections win unless the favorite's defense is entirely intact.
Do not treat Under 4.5 or Under totals as automatic safe cushions: short odds unders can still fail.
Back Under 3.5 in cup ties only when verified extreme squad rotation (missing value share >50%) suppresses offensive output.
football.summary: Refined and kept concrete lessons focusing on the success of positive Asian handicaps, lowering confidence instead of vetoing short-odds Over 1.5 and Under totals, and protecting 1X/X2 double chance selections.

lessons: Veto 1st half totals when the identical matchup is documented in recent mistakes, regardless of an overall winning family record (saved 2 of 2 losses).
Back 1st half Unders when the total line is below 120.0 points at odds 1.90 or higher (won 11 of 13); avoid or reduce stake on Unders at 120.5 or higher (won 2 of 3).
When the framework record for a betting family is LOSING, apply a downward adjustment to the model probability and back with lower confidence at odds of 1.90 or higher (won 4 of 4).
Do not back 1st half totals at odds below 1.90 unless the model probability exceeds 0.65.
Back NBA underdog handicaps (+1.5) with lower confidence when model probability exceeds 0.58, accepting odds between 1.70 and 1.85 (won 3 of 4).
nba.summary: Refined the record statistics for 1st half Under lines and NBA underdog handicaps to accurately reflect recent performance.

cognitive.lesson: High-probability bets can still lose to extreme scoring outliers; ensure model risk assessment accounts for tail-risk blowouts in high-total goal lines.
Even high-probability picks face random variance; never assume a bet is guaranteed despite an 80 percent base probability.
High-probability Over 1.5 bets can still fail due to normal match variance; maintain strict risk management even on strong model signals.
High-probability double chance bets can still fail due to normal match variance; always account for inherent draw risk in football.
Do not rely on high uncalibrated model probabilities without market validation for extreme handicap lines prone to blowouts.
High-probability models still lose to expected statistical variance; always manage risk even when Over 1.5 probability reaches 79%.
High probability picks near 79 percent will still lose roughly one out of five times due to standard statistical variance.
